\doxysubsection{Detailed Description}
Complex System Modeling Platform. 

configuration of Fraunhofer\textquotesingle{}s SAMG algebraic multigrid solver by string input.

enum to characterize possible phase states in the H2\+O-\/\+Na\+Cl phase diagram

a csmp-\/eigen interface solver class

The Complex System Modelling Platform (CSMP++) is an object-\/oriented finite-\/element based application programmer interface (API), designed for the simulation of complex geological processes and their interactions. CSMP++ is available on a license for commercial use, and is available for free to the academic user.

\Hypertarget{namespacecsmp_a0830e5b29bc2c16aa365209c6fc30e8f}\index{csmp@{csmp}!RockName@{RockName}}
\index{RockName@{RockName}!csmp@{csmp}}
\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{RockName}{RockName}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/3]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{namespacecsmp_a0830e5b29bc2c16aa365209c6fc30e8f} 
enum class \mbox{\hyperlink{namespacecsmp_a0830e5b29bc2c16aa365209c6fc30e8f}{csmp\+::\+Rock\+Name}} \+: int8\+\_\+t\hspace{0.3cm}{\ttfamily [strong]}}

Using the "{}tuple"{} container of different (rock) types, a mapping is created between the rocktype numbers sampled from Otway CRC3 and the names of the rock so that they can be seen during debugging.

The properties of the rocktypes are hard-\/coded into the corresponding classes \doxylink{structcsmp_1_1_c_r_c3___rock_type1}{CRC3\+\_\+\+Rock\+Type1} to 15.

The \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_heterogeneity_and_rate_aware_model}{Heterogeneity\+And\+Rate\+Aware\+Model} gets the rock types from the \textquotesingle{}rocktype\textquotesingle{} variable and choses the corresponding sets of curve fits.

For any of the composite rocktypes there are lamination parallel and perpendicular saturation functions. These are averaged dependent on the flow direction.

For composites, only the drainage curves are dependend on flow rate, the imbibition ones are not.

The imbibition curves are at the capillary limit.

Some of the composites are treated as mixtures between impermeable nonporous carbonate cemented rocks and single rock types. In these cases conventional relperms are used for the remaining porous subtypes, together with a downscaled porosity, and an anisotropic permeability. These are\+:

M\+\_\+\+Cb\+Sst\+\_\+\+Mst Massive bedding (Carbonate-\/cemented sandstone lamina and mudstone matrix) -\/ ONLY ONE SUBTYPE FLOWS M\+\_\+\+Cb\+Sst\+\_\+\+Slt Massive bedding (Carbonate-\/cemented sandstone lamina and siltstone matrix) -\/ ONLY ONE SUBTYPE FLOWS M\+\_\+\+Cb\+Sst\+\_\+\+FSs Massive bedding (Carbonate-\/cemented sandstone lamina and fine sandstone matrix) -\/ ONLY ONE SUBTYPE FLOWS M\+\_\+\+Cb\+Sst\+\_\+\+CSst Massive bedding (Carbonate-\/cemented sandstone lamina and coarse sandstone matrix) -\/ ONLY ONE SUBTYPE FLOWS

No flow will occur through\+:

H\+\_\+\+Cb\+Sst, // -- Homogeneous (Carbonate-\/cemented sandstone) -- NO\+\_\+\+FLOW

which leaves the 6 composites\+:

P\+\_\+\+Mst\+\_\+\+Slt, 4 COMPOSITE -- Planar bedding (Mudstone lamina and siltstone matrix) P\+\_\+\+Mst\+\_\+\+FSst, 6 COMPOSITE\+: Planar bedding (Mudstone lamina and fine sandstone matrix) P\+\_\+\+Mst\+\_\+\+CSst, // 8 COMPOSITE\+: Planar bedding (Mudstone lamina and coarse sandstone matrix) P\+\_\+\+Slt\+\_\+\+FSst, // 11 COMPOSITE\+: MAARTJE SAMPLE\# -\/ planar bedding (Siltstone lamina with fine sandstone matrix) P\+\_\+\+Slt\+\_\+\+CSst, // 12 COMPOSITE\+: Planar bedding (Siltstone lamina with coarse sandstone matrix) X\+\_\+\+CSst\+\_\+\+FSst, // 14 COMPOSITE\+: Cross bedding (Fine sandstone lamina and coarse sandstone matrix)

Then there are 4 rocktypes for which we can use standard VG / BC relperms\+:

H\+\_\+\+Mst, // -- Homogeneous Mudstone H\+\_\+\+Slt, // -- Homogeneous Siltstone H\+\_\+\+FSst, // -- Homogeneous (Fine Sandstone) H\+\_\+\+CSst // -- 15 Homogeneous (Coarse sandstone)

Those composite rocktypes where one of the components is carbonate cemented, can treated as single types with anisotropic perm and high irreducible sw

\begin{DoxyAttention}{Attention}
the averaging is not done inside of this class.
\end{DoxyAttention}

template$<$class T$>$ \\
bool csmp\+::binary\+File\+Read (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{std\+::fstream \&}]{fp}{, }\item[{std\+::deque$<$ std\+::vector$<$ T $>$ $>$ \&}]{stl\+\_\+ctner}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

Reads a vector of STL vector data from a binary file. The STL container is erased before adding the data, if it already contained any data. How many records are read is specified by an \textquotesingle{}unsigned long\textquotesingle{} number which precedes the dataset.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
A pointer to a binary file opened in read binary mode ("{}rb"{}), and a reference to an STL vector of vector.

\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
returns the boolean \textquotesingle{}true\textquotesingle{} if the number of data records which precedes the dataset in the file has been read correctly. If the file pointer is invalid or less data are read, the function returns false.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\hypertarget{namespacecsmp_implementation}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Implementation}{Implementation}}\label{namespacecsmp_implementation}
Uses the ANSI C function fread(). The vector\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<}\doxylink{classvector}{vector$<$\+T$>$} \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} which will hold the data is erased if it is not empty. Storage is reserved for the new number of elements which is read from file. Then the elements are read and the container is returned.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Application Examples}{Application Examples}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}
Efficiently read data into STL vector of vectors.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Messages}{Messages}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}
The function will return false if (1) the file pointer is invalid, (2) the number of data records cannot be read correctly, and (3) if this number does not match the number of records which were actually read. \Hypertarget{namespacecsmp_a40eb05f4d9692e7d3a8d4912a985c629}\index{csmp@{csmp}!binaryFileRead@{binaryFileRead}}

returns the 3D bounding box of the element 

Assuming the following numbering\+:

First tetra 0 1 2 3 -\/ ony one neighbor = nbr

Second tetra 0 4 1 2 -\/ 4 neigbors (inside of model)

The new elements are formed 1) 0 1 4 3 -\/ neighbors\+: 2 3 old-\/tet1-\/nbor 1 old-\/tet1-\/nbor 4 2) 1 2 4 3 -\/ neighbors\+: 3 1 old-\/tet1-\/nbor 0 old-\/tet2-\/nbor 0 3) 0 4 2 3 -\/ neighbors\+: 2 old-\/tet1-\/nbor 1 1 old-\/tet2-\/nbor 3

The corresponding neighbor elements are.

The operations will increase the number of elements by 1 for each corner processed because 2 elements are replaced by 3.

\begin{DoxyAttention}{Attention}
method returns without doing anything when all the nodes of the 2 tets are at the model boundary because, in that case, the connecting line between the corner and the extreme node of the inside tetrahedron will not go hrough the tetrahedra. As a consequence, degenerate tetrahedra would be produced by the splitting operation.
\end{DoxyAttention}

template$<$uint32\+\_\+t dim$>$ \\
bool csmp\+::build\+Regions\+Based\+On\+Property\+Range (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classcsmp_1_1_model}{Model}}$<$ dim $>$ \&}]{model}{, }\item[{std\+::set$<$ std\+::string $>$ \&}]{groups}{, }\item[{std\+::ifstream \&}]{ifs}{, }\item[{char \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{text\+\_\+line}{, }\item[{size\+\_\+t}]{line\+\_\+length}{, }\item[{bool}]{verbose}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



build Regions based on the range of particular property data ( a.\+k.\+a block1 ) 

This method allows the user to define regions on the basis of input data ranges and is used if the supplied finite element mesh has no region names associated with it.

The method reads Block 1 of the file structure outlined in the class documentation further below. The text string that it interprets for this purpose must have the form\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{joint\ \ \ tab\ \ \ \ \ permeability\ \ \ \ tab\ \ \ \ \ 1.0e-\/8\ 1.0e-\/8}

\end{DoxyCode}


Where the first string is that regionname that will be used, then comes the name of the variable whose range will be tested and then the range of variable values that shall discern the finite elements that will be accumulated into the intended region. Importantly, the variable that is used to form the region must be an element property because any region must have at least one element.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
The method takes a reference to the \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_model}{Model} object in which the region shall be created and the textline which contains the data on the basis of which the region shall be formed.

\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
The method returns the name of the newly created region into its third argument.
\end{DoxyReturn}
The method also returns the boolean variable true if the attempt to build the region was successful.\hypertarget{namespacecsmp_implementation}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Implementation}{Implementation}}\label{namespacecsmp_implementation}
The region is created directly so that it can be accessed immediately after the method is called provided that the call was successful.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Messages}{Messages}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}

Loops over the surface cells of the model subdomain, checking whether any of the projections of the normals of the neighbor cells onto the normal of the current element are negative.

\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
if any of the projections is negative, method returns false. A negative projection will mean that the normals of the neighboring cells are at \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} to 90\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}o to the current cell; this should not be the case unless the surface has cusps with in it.

if the region does not consist entirely of surface elements an error is reported.
\end{DoxyReturn}
\begin{DoxyAttention}{Attention}
even if the normals have a consistent orientation, this method may return false if the surface contains a cusp (\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}90\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}o kink).
\end{DoxyAttention}
\begin{DoxyRefDesc}{Test}
\item[\mbox{\hyperlink{test__test000048}{Test}}]SKM 30/3/2016 for 3D only\end{DoxyRefDesc}

collects pointers to Faces that may be needed to accumulate surface integrals on a computational domain consisting of elements 

Collects pointers to Faces that may be needed to accumulate surface integrals on the computational domain. Reports whether any faces were identified.

Two cases are considered\+:
\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item If the computational domain is \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_model}{Model}, all boundaries will be considered automatically and the \textquotesingle{}boundary\+\_\+faces\textquotesingle{} vector stays uninitialsed
\item When computations are performed on a model subdomain the Faces that share higher-\/dimensional elements with it are recorded.
\end{DoxyEnumerate}

\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
reports on whether a Face\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} vector was initialised 
\end{DoxyReturn}

Computes the CO2 saturation value above which there a wedge of CO2 reaches from the lowest point of the FV to the highest point. Method uses \textquotesingle{}vertical extent\textquotesingle{} and \textquotesingle{}finite volume diameter\textquotesingle{} in this calculation.

The scalar node variable \textquotesingle{}spill-\/point saturation\textquotesingle{} is computed from the ratio of the (approximate) volume of CO2 required to create CO2 pool that spans its diameter in the dip direction and its pre-\/computed (exact total) \textquotesingle{}finite volume\textquotesingle{}.

check whether through modification of the manifold, the original topology identifier is no longer valid 

Checks whether the current topologic classification of the combination of nodes within one \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_node_manifold}{Node\+Manifold} makes sense, using the number of collocated nodes and their geometric attributes as evaluation criteria. Assigns classification that adds \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_split_boundary}{Split\+Boundary} specific features.

What can be distinguished here? -\/ To start with the nodes have the attributes, see \doxylink{_c_s_m_p__global__enumerations_8h_source}{CSMP\+\_\+global\+\_\+enumerations.\+h}\+:

VERTEX\+\_\+\+POINT, ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} a point within the model volume INTERSECTION\+\_\+\+POINT,///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} a point where lines cross or multiple surfaces intersect PERIMETER\+\_\+\+POINT, ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} point at the end of a line inside a 2D model EXTERIOR\+\_\+\+POINT, ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} on an outside surface of the model INTERIOR\+\_\+\+LINE, ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} a line on the interior of the model PERIMETER\+\_\+\+LINE, ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} on a surface edge inside of the model EXTERIOR\+\_\+\+LINE, ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} an edge of the model INTERSECTION\+\_\+\+LINE, ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} belonging to multiple surfaces INTERIOR\+\_\+\+SURFACE, ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} a surface withing the model PERIMETER\+\_\+\+SURFACE, ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} a surface forming the hull of an object inside of the model EXTERIOR\+\_\+\+SURFACE ///\texorpdfstring{$<$}{<} a surface delimiting the model

In which way does a Node\+Manifold\+Type go beyond these classifications? \begin{DoxyVerb} - classification that applies to the group of nodes united in the manifold
 - indication of a SplitBoundary (but this is already done by having a node manifold)
 - specifics lie the distinction of a point on a line ending in 3D space from a perimeter point om a line boundary in 2D
 - intersection between (multiple) split boundaries
 - intersection between boundary and SplitBoundary
 - intersection points between a line and a splitboundary LINE_SPLITBOUNDARY_INTERSECTION
\end{DoxyVerb}


What are the possible combinations of BREP TOPOTYPES distinguishing different types of manifolds?


\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item collocated point (2D, not a splitboundary), and line splitboundaries (3D) = as many nodes as parent elements of the line-\/element node
\item crossing points -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} 4 nodes for 2 lines in 2D \& 3D, 5 nodes for 3, 6 nodes for 4...
\item surface intersections -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} only in 3D\+: 4 nodes where 2 splitboundaries cross
\item three nodes -\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>} T intersection in 2D
\end{DoxyEnumerate}\hypertarget{namespacecsmp_autotoc_md10}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Consistency Checks performed, using set$<$\+TOPOTYPE$>$\+:}{Consistency Checks performed, using set$<$\+TOPOTYPE$>$\+:}}\label{namespacecsmp_autotoc_md10}

\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item If all the nodes in the set have the same \doxylink{group___c_s_m_p__global__enumerations_ga65b4b9788928fc2599d5cc1d1960942a}{TOPOTYPE}, consistency is achieved and the \doxylink{group___c_s_m_p__global__enumerations_gaaf964c39623dfdbf0a48242aaa1253e9}{Manifold\+Type} is determined
\item If the nodes have different types, each node is checked to see whether the \doxylink{group___c_s_m_p__global__enumerations_ga65b4b9788928fc2599d5cc1d1960942a}{TOPOTYPE} clashes with the actual geometry that it forms part of. For the potentially corrected classifications a re-\/evaluation of the \doxylink{group___c_s_m_p__global__enumerations_gaaf964c39623dfdbf0a48242aaa1253e9}{Manifold\+Type} is performed.
\item \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_split_boundary}{Split\+Boundary} specific criteria are considered to distinguish basic intersections from boundary intersections from splitboundary intersections

{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{namespacecsmp_a9696b64d80011d85ead8bb535c51519f} 
\mbox{\hyperlink{classcsmp_1_1_point}{Point}}$<$ 2U $>$ csmp\+::cross\+Product (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classcsmp_1_1_point}{Point}}$<$ 2U $>$ \&}]{p1}{, }\item[{const \mbox{\hyperlink{classcsmp_1_1_point}{Point}}$<$ 2U $>$ \&}]{p2}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

cross\+Product(2\+D)

Watch out in 2D the cross product is not uniquely defined\+:

Cross\+Product\+Analog1(\+U,\+V)=(U.\+x\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}V.y-\/\+U.\+y\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}V.x) is a scalar! Cross\+Product\+Analog2(\+U)=(U.\+y, -\/\+U.\+x) (yes, second analog takes only one argument, and return orthogonal vector \+:) First analog makes some physical and geometrical sense, second analog comes from "{}determinant rule"{}, for determinant of 2x2 matrix,

\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}A B\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}C D\texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} = AD-\/\+BC

To avoid ambiguities, NAN is returned in the second component of \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_point}{Point}. \Hypertarget{namespacecsmp_ab039fb02536702957d29d762fb53866c}\index{csmp@{csmp}!CSMP\_NO\_DATA\_VALUE@{CSMP\_NO\_DATA\_VALUE}}

\Hypertarget{namespacecsmp_aae47fa4d57dcce94531fa12136ea67ff}\index{csmp@{csmp}!delta\_X\_FromFV\_Volume@{delta\_X\_FromFV\_Volume}}
\index{delta\_X\_FromFV\_Volume@{delta\_X\_FromFV\_Volume}!csmp@{csmp}}
\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{delta\_X\_FromFV\_Volume()}{delta\_X\_FromFV\_Volume()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{namespacecsmp_aae47fa4d57dcce94531fa12136ea67ff} 
double csmp\+::delta\+\_\+\+X\+\_\+\+From\+FV\+\_\+\+Volume (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{double}]{FV\+\_\+volume}{, }\item[{uint32\+\_\+t}]{dim}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

Calculates the critical tranport distance in the direction of flow delta x from the volume of the finite-\/volume cell under the assumption that the FV cell is spherical. For this case this distance is equivalent to the diameter of the sphere d = 2 (3 V / 4 pi)\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}1/3 where V is the FV volume.

For skewed elements this method may fail, but it should give a rather conservative estimate for the case where the element is elongated in the direction of the flow.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
The method needs the volume of the current FV cell as input.

\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
The method returns the diameter of the hypothetically spherical FV cell. 
\end{DoxyReturn}

\end{DoxyReturn}

\end{DoxyAttention}

gradient limiter for the solution of diffusion equations with the FVM method 

Computes limiter values in the case when diffusive fluxes are incorporated into the higher order transport scheme.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}

Notes

\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{doesDomainsFileExist()}{doesDomainsFileExist()}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{namespacecsmp_a0b7e5947eda4d98de589eaae04a32172} 
bool csmp\+::does\+Domains\+File\+Exist (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const char \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{regions\+\_\+file}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



read regions from file 

Reduce\+To\+Domains() reads an ASCII (text) input file to determine the names of the model regions that shall be retained by the current model toopology. The name of the input file is created from the user supplied character string by appending \textquotesingle{}-\/regions.\+txt\textquotesingle{}.

The regions file consists of the following\+:


\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item headline with file name, model name etc.
\item properties whose specific values shall be listed after region name (here the tab key separates the property names which can contain whitespace). At least, the property \textquotesingle{}permeability\textquotesingle{} must be specified.
\end{DoxyEnumerate}

If the file is used only to identify the regions of interest, the second line and the property information in the later part of the file will be ignored. Still the second line is treated as if it would contain property data. No region names can be specified in it. We recommend to write \textquotesingle{}no property data\textquotesingle{} into the second line to clarify if the file is only used to select output regions.


\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item model regions followed by property values (after the last property value in each line, arbitrary comments can be placed but will be ignored)
\end{DoxyEnumerate}


\begin{DoxyParams}{Parameters}
{\em regions\+\_\+file} & The name of the regions file for which an extension \textquotesingle{}-\/regions.\+txt\textquotesingle{} is appended. ~\newline
\\
\hline
\end{DoxyParams}

Elements on the inside of this domain are enlisted first in the output Element-\/face number pairs. If neither of the elements is found in the model subdomain, an error is reported.

\end{DoxyParams}

finds the neighbors of dim-\/1 element, and their faces that connect to it; index records neighbor materials 

\doxylink{namespacecsmp_ad5202c6b521360ae1a186a5452878a3c}{higher\+Dimensional\+Neighbors()} is used by Create\+Internal\+Boundary\+From( dim-\/minus1-\/region...) and for a similar method which creates a \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_split_boundary}{Split\+Boundary}.

\doxylink{namespacecsmp_ad5202c6b521360ae1a186a5452878a3c}{higher\+Dimensional\+Neighbors()} -\/ finds the higher-\/dim neighbor elements of a dim-\/1 element embedded within the higher-\/dim mesh.


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item finds the IDs of the higher dimensional neighbors of the current lower-\/dimensional element
\item identifies which of the neighbors is on the inside and which on the outside as indicated by the normal direction of the lower dimensional element
\item identifies the materials on either side
\end{DoxyItemize}

\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
two inside-\/outside pairs of element idx numbers and corresponding materials on either side all the data are stored in the returnd \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_face_construction_data}{Face\+Construction\+Data} object.
\end{DoxyReturn}
assumptions
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item assumes that the nodes and elements in the entire model domain are numbered continuously
\end{DoxyItemize}

application
\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item use this function for finding neighbors of a surface element that sits on the inside of another region

\begin{DoxyAttention}{Attention}
both neighbors have to be present for this to work.
\end{DoxyAttention}
TODO\+: if speed becomes critical, perhaps refactor using set\+\_\+intersection() on nodes of elements
\end{DoxyItemize}

taking into account element thickness and total velocity, initialises\+: finite volume, sector volume, sector pore volume, FV pore volume, facet area, facet normal, facet flux, flux balance.

We store the volume of the finite volumes and their pore volumes


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item finite volume
\item finite volume (effective) pore volume
\item sector volume (stored at sector integration point)
\item sector weight\+: sector pore volume / finite volume pore volume = weighting factor
\end{DoxyItemize}

Reads file with the mapping from integer codes to region names and creates corresponding model regions. Elements with property identifiers that are not contained in the regions file are ignore, but the unrecognised codes are reported to screen and file. The file has the following format\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{headline\ (printed\ to\ screen)}
\DoxyCodeLine{identifier\ value\ \ tab\ \ region\ name\ (can\ contain\ white\ space)}

\end{DoxyCode}


\begin{DoxyAttention}{Attention}
if the rocktype file info file is omitted, the function will search for a file called\+: "{}model\+\_\+name-\/property-\/identifiers.\+txt"{}
\end{DoxyAttention}
\begin{DoxyNote}{Note}
only the first 2 tokens in each line of the file are read, allowing the user to add comments afterwards
\end{DoxyNote}

SKM

prints the face normals scaled by element size to file 

Loops over the faces of the element, collecting the (outward-\/pointing) face normals for display in VTK. Each normal is scaled by the sqrt of the element volume and placed with its origin on the barycenter of the corresponding face.

method calls Unit\+Normal\+To\+Face(size\+\_\+t face) to compute the unit normals.

prints the supplied node variable data DATA(dim x nodes) to file 

Outputs supplied nodal values of a variable into an output file which can be visualized with the visualization toolkit VTK. The file is in text format. The ID of the parent element as well as the extension "{}.\+vtk"{} will be appended to the output file name. ~\newline
\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
The name of the data file and the name of the variable as it is later used in VTK must be supplied as output arguments. The third argument is a data matrix which will contain n-\/colums=nodes and n-\/rows = dimensions of data (n-\/rows=1 = scalar data, n-\/rows=3 = \doxylink{classvector}{vector$<$double$>$} data etc.) of nodal variable data. ~\newline
\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Application Examples}{Application Examples}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}
Single elements are output to VTK in order to test the quality of interpolation and the computed properties directly. ~\newline
\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Messages}{Messages}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}
The method will indicate if there is a problem in opening the output file. \Hypertarget{namespacecsmp_a777a8a78f3d3790d05cfc2a511a942c8}\index{csmp@{csmp}!outputRegionBoundaryToVTK@{outputRegionBoundaryToVTK}}

void csmp\+::parallel\+Plate\+Permeability\+From\+Channel\+Width (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classcsmp_1_1_model}{Model}}$<$ dim $>$ \&}]{sg}{, }\item[{const char \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{channel\+\_\+region}{, }\item[{const char \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{channel\+\_\+width}{ = {\ttfamily "{}channel~width"{}}, }\item[{double}]{minimum\+\_\+channel\+\_\+width}{ = {\ttfamily 1.0e-\/9}}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

Computes the parallel-\/plate permeability and the channel width in the channel region. The aperture amounts to the maximum width of the channel at any particular segment. The results are stored in the variables \textquotesingle{}permeability\textquotesingle{} (m2) and \textquotesingle{}channel width\textquotesingle{} (m). ~\newline


The calculated permeability is k = a\texorpdfstring{$^\wedge$}{\string^}2/12 where a is the channel width.

Solves the Laplace equation with a source term of 1 to find find the maximum transect across the target region by means of differentiation.

Finds the 2 higher-\/dim parent elements that share face identified by its nodes, inner element is reported first; outer next; face-\/nodes of dim-\/1 element must be in correct order.

\Hypertarget{namespacecsmp_a879b22fcd55025a2e812db4ee6faddfa}\index{csmp@{csmp}!pointPropertyMapping@{pointPropertyMapping}}
\index{pointPropertyMapping@{pointPropertyMapping}!csmp@{csmp}}
\doxysubsubsection{\texorpdfstring{pointPropertyMapping()}{pointPropertyMapping()}\hspace{0.1cm}{\footnotesize\ttfamily [1/2]}}
{\footnotesize\ttfamily \label{namespacecsmp_a879b22fcd55025a2e812db4ee6faddfa} 
void csmp\+::point\+Property\+Mapping (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{const std\+::string \&}]{model\+\_\+name}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}

Maps point properties from point clouds tagged with region names to current 3D CSMP model.

Properties are mapped either to volumes and / or surfaces, but the latter must be assigned last to avoid overwriting of pre-\/assigned values.

After successful property assignment, the model is output to VTU for examination. If appropriate the results can be safed to current CSMP binary.

The mapping involves both, volume/surface averaging, when multiple points fall into the same element, interpolation using the SAMG solver when the data are sparse, or nearest neighbor interpolation if where there are isolated element without property values.

See Mosser (2013, SPE 167629 -\/STU) for a full description of the implemented algorithm.

prints range to screen; returns either min(arg=false) or maximum variable value (default) 

Method obtains the range of values for the physical variable that it is prompted for by the user. For vector and tensor variables, the length and the minimum/maximum eigenvalues are returned (check whether the latter actually happens).

With the optional boolean argument (default=true), the user can determin the return value. As the default, the maximum obtained value is returned; else the minimum.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
The model to be examined, the name of the target physical variable, and targeted return value (true-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}maximum, false-\/\texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}minimum of target variable).

The second version of this method also takes an I/O handler as argument in order to log the calculated values to file etc.

\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Either the maximum (default) or the minimum value of the target variable. The result is printed to the screen. 
\end{DoxyReturn}

in order to get canonical numbering lets perform suitable rotation. in case of vertex 6 having 1 diagonal we want face with this diagonal on the right in case of vertex 6 having 2 diagonals we want face adjacent to those 2 on the rigth as well in case of vertex 6 hvaing 0 or 3 diagonals we keep the positions of faces

120 rotation over the diagonal 06

using random number generator, adds percentage of Gaussian noise to variable values 

Randomly perturbs the values of a scalar target property by subtracting an amount which varies between minus zero and the specified percentage of the original maximum value of the target property.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
Random\+Perturb() requires the name of the property which shall be perturbed and the percentage of the original maximum value of the property by which the property shall be perturbed, in order to operate.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Application Examples}{Application Examples}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}
Processes which are critically dependent on initial conditions can profit from a \textquotesingle{}noisy\textquotesingle{} input signal when one tries to simulate natural behaviour.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Messages}{Messages}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}

Read\+Boundary\+Property\+Values\+And\+Conditions\hypertarget{namespacecsmp_autotoc_md9}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Example}{Example}}\label{namespacecsmp_autotoc_md9}
Sets variable at the boundary of interest to the values and conditions imposed in the textline. 
\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ a\ fluid\ pressure\ of\ 200\ bar\ is\ assigned\ to\ the\ interior\ of\ a\ boundary\ named}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ 'BOUNDARY3'}}
\DoxyCodeLine{BOUNDARY3\ \ \ tab\ interior\ tab\ \mbox{\hyperlink{group___c_s_m_p__global__enumerations_gga98d2031b830da37499a1b512d9dca4b9a2d373b048f997a96c661862c40f2fcae}{DIRICH}}\ tab\ fluid\ pressure\ \ tab\ \ \ 2.0E+7}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ TOP\ is\ assigned\ values\ for\ the\ vector\ variable\ 'displacement}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ Dirichlet\ names\ the\ condition\ that\ is\ applied;\ however\ only\ to\ the\ Y-\/component}}
\DoxyCodeLine{TOP\ complete\ \ \ \ Dirichlet\ \ \ displacement\ \ \ \ Plain\ \ \ Dirichlet\ \ \ Plain\ \ \ 0.\ \ -\/4.356\ \ 0.}

\end{DoxyCode}


\begin{DoxyAttention}{Attention}
Note the duplicate use of flags in the case of vector or tensor properties. The first flag specifies which flag the method shall not overwrite in case a value is already set to this flag at the boundary. This controls the situation, for instance, where nodes that are shared among multiple boundaries have already been set a Dirichlet constraint for one of the vector components while the other is still up for assignment. Setting the first flag to Dirichlet allows this because it signals to the method not to overwrite preexisting Dirichlet constraints (anywhere on the boundary).

This applies only to unique boundaries.

In case of vector and tensor variables, flags are assigned to each component. This means whatever was on the boundary before is overwritten. 
\end{DoxyAttention}

read box boundary values and conditions ( a.\+k.\+a. block4 ) 

This method reads data of the type Block 4, see class documentation below. It assigns boundary conditions to a the supplied box-\/shaped model. Any of the \doxylink{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_ga8e4421c3cd02f67e535bceb2dc74bfb6}{BOX\+\_\+\+BOUNDARY} enumeration switches may be used to specify the boundary conditions. The input should have the following form\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ a\ uniform\ (scalar)\ fluid\ pressure\ value\ is\ applied\ to\ a\ line\ 2D\ model}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ BOX\_BOUNDARY\ \ \ condition\ \ \ \ \ \ variable\ name\ \ \ variable\ values}}
\DoxyCodeLine{TOP\ \ \ \ \ tab\ \ \ \ \ Dirichlet\ \ \ tab\ fluid\ pressure\ \ tab\ 1.0\ 1.0}
\DoxyCodeLine{}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ 2D\ model,\ (vector)\ variable\ velocity\ with\ x,\ y\ components\ specified\ for}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ the\ 2\ endpoints\ of\ the\ linear\ boundary.\ The\ x\ component\ is\ fixed,\ the}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ y\ component\ can\ be\ modified\ by\ the\ computation.\ The\ PLAIN\ condition}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ flag\ is\ ignored\ since\ velocity\ is\ a\ vector\ property}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ the\ flags\ after\ the\ variable\ values\ specifiy\ the\ desired\ condition}}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{preprocessor}{\#\ flags\ for\ the\ x\ and\ y\ velocity\ components}}
\DoxyCodeLine{LEFT\ \ \ \ \mbox{\hyperlink{group___c_s_m_p__global__enumerations_gga98d2031b830da37499a1b512d9dca4b9adba268ba55a652b1efcdd9338882eca6}{PLAIN}}\ \ \ velocity\ \ \ \ 5.\ \ 0.\ \ 5.\ \ 0.\ \ Dirichlet\ \ \ Plain}

\end{DoxyCode}


Importantly, behind the values that shall be assigned to end points of the linear boundary (2D) or the corner points of the planar boundary in 3D only two or three flags can / must be specified. These overwrite the boundary condition flag specified earlier in the line in the case where the property is a vector or tensor variable the individual components of which should be treatable separately.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
The method takes a reference to the \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_model}{Model} representing the box shaped model to which the boundary condition shall be applied to.\hypertarget{namespacecsmp_implementation}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Implementation}{Implementation}}\label{namespacecsmp_implementation}
Thus far assignments can only be made for scalar and vector type CSP basic variables.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Application Examples}{Application Examples}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}
Only for box-\/shaped models or models with an irregular top surface. In this latter case TOP must not be used but the boundary can be accessed if was properly assigned an IRREGULAR flag instead.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Messages}{Messages}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}

read default property values ( a.\+k.\+a block2 ) 

This method reads data of the type Block 2, see class documentation below. It assigns default values to the entire model. These values are interpreted from the supplied input string that should have the form\+:


\begin{DoxyCode}{0}
\DoxyCodeLine{\textcolor{keyword}{property}\ name\ \ tab\ \ value(s)}

\end{DoxyCode}


The input property value is compared with the physically meaningful range that the user specified in the \textquotesingle{}\texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}-\/variables.txt\textquotesingle{} file. If this range is exceeded, the value will be corrected to the nearest of the two extrema.

Dependent on whether the property is a scalar, vector, or tensor variable a different number of values are expected as input. This number also depends on the spatial dimension of the model (a vector has 2 components in 2D, but 3 in 3D, a 2D tensor is 2 x 2 and a 3D one 3 x 3 in size).\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
The method assigns the correctly parsed property value to its first argument -\/ a \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_model}{Model} object. The second argument is character string that should contain the tab-\/separated variable name and value(s).\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Messages}{Messages}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}

Reading ZCORN block (indices of the pillars).

\begin{DoxyAttention}{Attention}
Recall that X points to the east, Y points to the south, Z point downwards. The coordinates of cell corners are written layer by layer and can be denoted by NW,NE,SW,SE.
\end{DoxyAttention}
\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+\+\_\+X ( EAST ) \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|}\textbackslash{} \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} \textbackslash{} NW --- NE \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} \textbackslash{} \textbackslash{} \textbackslash{} \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} \textbackslash{} SW --- SE \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} \textbackslash{} ( DOWNWARD )Z \texorpdfstring{$\vert$}{|} \textbackslash{}Y ( SOUTH )

Format\+: ZCONR z(1,1,1)top,NW z(1,1,1)top,NE z(2,1,1)top,NW z(2,1,1)top,NE ... z(\+NX,1,1)top,NW z(\+NX,1,1)top,NE "{}= cycle 0 with idy =0"{} z(1,1,1)top,SW z(1,1,1)top,SE z(2,1,1)top,SW z(2,1,1)top,SE ... z(\+NX,1,1)top,SW z(\+NX,1,1)top,SE "{}= cycle 1 with idx =0"{} z(1,2,1)top,NW z(1,2,1)top,NE z(2,2,1)top,NW z(2,2,1)top,NE ... z(\+NX,2,1)top,NW z(\+NX,2,1)top,NE "{}= cycle 0 with idy =1"{} z(1,2,1)top,SW z(1,2,1)top,SE z(2,2,1)top,SW z(2,2,1)top,SE ... z(\+NX,2,1)top,SW z(\+NX,2,1)top,SE "{}= cycle 1 with idx =1"{}z(1,\+NY,1)top,SW z(1,\+NY,1)top,SE z(2,\+NY,1)top,SW z(2,\+NY,1)top,SE ... z(\+NX,\+NY,1)top,SW z(\+NX,\+NY,1)top,SE z(1,1,1)btm,NW z(1,1,1)btm,NE z(2,1,1)btm,NW z(2,1,1)btm,NE ... z(\+NX,1,1)btm,NW z(\+NX,1,1)btm,NEz(1,\+NY,1)btm,SW z(1,\+NY,1)btm,SE z(2,\+NY,1)btm,SW z(2,\+NY,1)btm,SE ... z(\+NX,\+NY,1)btm,SW z(\+NX,\+NY,1)btm,SE z(1,1,2)top,NW z(1,1,2)top,NE z(2,1,2)top,NW z(2,1,2)top,NE ... z(\+NX,1,2)top,NW z(\+NX,1,2)top,NEz(1,\+NY,\+NZ)btm,SW z(1,\+NY,\+NZ)btm,SE z(2,\+NY,\+NZ)btm,SW z(2,\+NY,\+NZ)btm,SE ... z(\+NX,\+NY,\+NZ)btm,SW z(\+NX,\+NY,\+NZ)btm,SE 4 cycles\+: cycle 0\+: top NW-\/\+NE cycle 1\+: top SW-\/\+SE cycle 2\+: btm NW-\/\+NE cycle 3\+: btm SW-\/\+SE

void csmp\+::strip\+Domain\+Edges\+For (\begin{DoxyParamCaption}\item[{\mbox{\hyperlink{classcsmp_1_1_model}{Model}}$<$ 2U $>$ \&}]{sg}{, }\item[{const char \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*}}]{el\+\_\+prop}{}\end{DoxyParamCaption})}



for \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_triangulator}{Triangulator} meshes\+: for meshes created from pixels, finds outlier triangles (3 nodes at region boundaries) and flips their property values 

Strip\+Domain\+Edges\+For() tests the spatial distribution of a scalar input element property for outliers and removes these. Property outliers are elements that constitute a property value boundary with \texorpdfstring{$>$}{>}=two of their faces. When such elements are detected, their property value is set to the average of the surrounding elements. The property is changed only if the outside property is either smaller or greater than the element property.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
The name of the property whose variations over the mesh shall be defined by relatively smooth boundaries.\hypertarget{namespacecsmp_implementation}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Implementation}{Implementation}}\label{namespacecsmp_implementation}
The method using the connections among elements to test whether the element represents a property outlier.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Application Examples}{Application Examples}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_enums_application}
The method is used for regular meshes which were created from pixel-\/type input data. In this case the method allows to capitalize on the element splits which were created by the \doxylink{classcsmp_1_1_triangulator}{Triangulator} meshing tool along property boundaries. The result are boundaries with 45o segments that superseed the stepwise property boundaries of the original mesh.

Numerous calls to Strip\+Domain\+Edges\+For() also allow to erode regions defined by stepwise property variations.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Messages}{Messages}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}
The method will always warn the user that the model properties are modified. If the target property is not an element property, the simulation will be halted by a fatal error.

If the target property is not a scalar variable the method will return without modifying the target property and it will report a warning. Here is the call graph for this function\+:

The method needs access to the current model and the user should specify the precision with which the results shall be output. While a smaller precision makes the results more readable, remember that the plotted numbers will have been rounded up or down accordingly.

Function needs the nodal variable fluid pressure to be defined.\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Messages}{Messages}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_messages}

Matthai et al. 2009 (TIPM) explains theta limiting concept. 

When looping over the faces, this function computes temporal limiter values at each face(=segment) in this formulation).\hypertarget{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}{}\doxysubsection{\texorpdfstring{Input Arguments}{Input Arguments}}\label{group___c_s_m_pglobal_functions_arguments}
Input are values of the advected property psi at u=upwind, c=current, d=downwind FV cells. Notation\+:


\begin{DoxyItemize}
\item vol\+\_\+upstr, vol\+\_\+dwstr are volumes of control volumes i and j sharing the face
\item hf\+\_\+t0, hf\+\_\+t1\+: value of higher order flux (flux \texorpdfstring{$\ast$}{*} slope-\/limited advected quantity) across face at time t and t+1
\item dt\+: time increment value dt
\item vol\+\_\+upstr, vol\+\_\+dwstr\+: pore volume represented by the finite volume
\item cval\+\_\+t0, cval\+\_\+t1\+: value of advected quantity of current FV cell at t and t+dt
\item dval\+\_\+t0, dval\+\_\+t1\+: value of advected quantity of downstream FV cell at t and t+dt
\item method is implemented exactly like in the paper
\end{DoxyItemize}

\begin{DoxyReturn}{Returns}
Method returns the temporally limited segment values of the advected property. 
\end{DoxyReturn}

Adjusts halo cells and perimeter node parent-\/element vectors in mesh domains which is going to be deleted; this domain is identified by supplied range of iterators. 

Method supports the deletion a set of finite elements from your mesh, locally updating the connectivity of the remaining elements, while it tries to minimize the number of operations by focusing only on the immediate neighbors of the elements being deleted.

Step-\/by-\/\+Step Algorithm


\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item Mark the Elements for Deletion\+: A unique negative region ID of -\/999 is assigned to each element that will be deleted. This attribute allows to identify deleted elements without affecting other mesh operations.
\item Identify the Halo Neighbors of the Deleted Elements\+: • For each element in the set to be deleted, iterate over its neighbors (from the std\+::vector of neighbor pointers). • For each face, if the neighboring element on that face is not marked for deletion, mark it as a “halo element” for updating or collect a pointer to it in a separate container as it needs to have its connectivity adjusted.
\item Update the Connectivity of Halo Elements\+: • For each halo neighbor identified in the previous step, iterate over its list of neighbors (the neighbor pointers for each face). • For each face with a neighbor that is marked for deletion, set the corresponding neighbor pointer to nullptr because this connection will become invalid.

\begin{DoxyRefDesc}{Todo}
\item[\mbox{\hyperlink{todo__todo000163}{Todo}}]If the face with the deleted neighbor belongs to a lower dimensional element, it may be a manfold that is potentially connected to other remaining element(s). In this case, replace the deleted neighbor that will be deleted with another adjacent lower-\/dimensional element sharing its face nodes. This requires searching because there is no knowledge stored about face-\/node sharing alternative neighbors.\end{DoxyRefDesc}

\end{DoxyEnumerate}

Now that these tasks have been completed one can\+:


\begin{DoxyEnumerate}
\item Delete the Elements from the Mesh\+: • Now that the border neighbors have been updated, you can safely delete the elements in the set marked for deletion.
\item Clean-\/\+Up Neighbor Pointers\+: • Remove any redundant or invalid pointers from the std\+::vector of neighbor pointers in each element to ensure the integrity of your mesh data structure.
\end{DoxyEnumerate}

\begin{DoxyAttention}{Attention}
function assumes that all elements in the iterator range have the same dimension, i.\+e. are lines, surfaces or volumes
\end{DoxyAttention}

\item Delete the Elements from the Mesh\+: • Now that the border neighbors have been updated, you can safely delete the elements in the set marked for deletion.
\item Clean-\/\+Up Neighbor Pointers\+: • Remove any redundant or invalid pointers from the std\+::vector of neighbor pointers in each element to ensure the integrity of your mesh data structure.
\end{DoxyEnumerate}

\begin{DoxyAttention}{Attention}
function assumes that all elements in the iterator range have the same dimension, i.\+e. are lines, surfaces or volumes
\end{DoxyAttention}
